$comment: Authoritative record of every NEXT_PUBLIC_* the web app consumes, and how each one
reaches production. Enforced by scripts/ops/web-build-inputs.test.ts, which fails CI
when a consumed variable is missing here, when an entry here has no consumer, and when
a client-consumed variable is not supplied to the CI web build.
WHY THIS EXISTS: NEXT_PUBLIC_* is NOT simply 'client = build-time, server = runtime'.
The real rule, verified against the built artifact, is: SET AT BUILD => folded into a
literal everywhere; UNSET AT BUILD => left as a process.env lookup. On the server that
lookup reads the live process env, so it appears to work. In the BROWSER the same lookup
resolves against an empty process shim and is undefined forever. Setting such a variable
in prod .env and reloading PM2 therefore changes the server and cannot change the
ecosystem.config.js re-injects NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID into the web process at PM2
start for exactly that reason, and it cannot work for a client component. It is harmless
today only because the value is empty on prod.

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
variables.defaultIfAbsent: differs by consumer, deliberately recorded in full: (1) lib/api/client.ts falls back to http://localhost:3000/api/v1 on its server branch and warns in production; lib/server-api.ts falls back to the same value unconditionally, with no branch and no warning; (2) the display client components (DisplayClient.tsx, ContentRenderer.tsx, ContentScreen.tsx) fall back to window.location.origin; (3) next.config.js omits two images.remotePatterns entries; (4) next.config.security.js omits the origin from CSP connect-src/img-src/media-src.
variables.why: Consumer (2) is not merely a URL default -- apiOrigin joins baseOrigin in the Set that gates whether a device token is appended to a device-content/*/file URL (DisplayClient.tsx authenticateDisplayContentUrl). Absent, that set narrows to the page origin, so this variable participates in a trust decision and not only in addressing. next.config.security.js additionally rejects a loopback origin in a production build.

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL
variables.defaultIfAbsent: differs by consumer: lib/hooks/useSocket.ts falls back to http://localhost:3002 in development and to the EMPTY STRING in production, which engine.io resolves to location.hostname/port (same-origin); app/display/hooks/useDeviceConnection.ts falls back UNCONDITIONALLY to http://localhost:3002 with no production branch -- on a display device that would attempt a loopback connection.
variables.why: Feeds the browser socket connection and the CSP connect-src. next.config.security.js THROWS when it is unset in a production build, so the same-origin empty-string path is unreachable in a real prod build -- but useSocket still implements it, and that behaviour must be preserved if the interlock ever changes.

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN
variables.defaultIfAbsent: every sentry helper no-ops via `if (!dsn) return`
variables.why: Sentry is a stub: @sentry/nextjs is not a dependency of web/package.json and initSentry() has no call site. Supplying a DSN would not start reporting. Setting this must be part of actually wiring Sentry, not a config change on its own.

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_SCHEDULES_ENABLED
variables.defaultIfAbsent: false -- the read is a strict `=== 'true'`, so absent/empty/'1'/'TRUE' are all false
variables.why: The schedules feature is off. Prod .env carries NEXT_PUBLIC_SCHEDULES_ENABLED=false, which matches the default, so server and client agree today. Turning it on is a BUILD input: setting it only in prod .env would enable the server-rendered page while every client nav guard stayed false.

variables.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID
variables.defaultIfAbsent: the GoogleSignInButton EFFECT early-returns, so the GSI script never loads and no button is rendered into the ref. The component itself still renders its container div (deliberately, to avoid an SSR/client hydration mismatch), collapsed to 0 height.
variables.why: Google Sign-In is not configured: prod .env has NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID= (empty). ENABLING IT REQUIRES A CI BUILD INPUT. ecosystem.config.js reads it from web/.env.local (NOT the root .env, despite its own comment) and injects it at PM2 start -- that reaches the SSR process only; the browser bundle reads an empty process shim and the button stays hidden with no error anywhere. So editing the root .env does nothing at all, and editing web/.env.local does nothing the user can see.
